evidence.note: Second-hand: result reported by this review from Kim et al., JACS 2026 (ref 12); curate value objects from the cited work itself.

props.scope: Cu electrocatalysts in CO2RR; Kim et al., JACS 2026 (ref 12).
props.statement: Two distinct Cu reconstruction pathways operate during CO2RR: surface oxide formation, where CuOx species form transient active sites for C2+ that are reduced cathodically, and potential-induced metal dissolution into Cu2+ with redeposition under cathodic conditions, which renews the catalytic interface; adding trace Cu2+ to the electrolyte builds such a dynamic interface and sustains C2+ generation without anodic pulsing.

props.statement: During CO2RR on Cu(111), specific adsorption of OH- on terrace sites drives the ejection of undercoordinated Cu adatoms from the lattice, and the isolated adatoms are captured and stabilized by adsorbed *CO.

props.statement: On Cu under CO electroreduction, a mixed adlayer of adsorbed CO and kinetically trapped OH lifts surface Cu atoms into metastable CuCO(OH)n complexes, turning flat terraces into low-coordinated Cu nanoclusters; at more cathodic potentials (below about -0.5 VRHE) rapid CO consumption destabilizes these clusters, which ripen, aggregate or dissolve into monatomic islands and surface vacancies while OH stays trapped on the roughened surface.

props.statement: GIXAS/GIXRD showed that the surface Cu oxide layer of polycrystalline Cu electrodes is fully reduced to metallic Cu before the CO2RR onset potential, and that surface reconstruction proceeds preferentially towards (100) facets in the presence of CO2.

props.name: Anodic pulses reset Cu, ethylene lifetime x20

evidence.note: Second-hand: result reported by this review from Kok et al., JACS 2024 (ref 45); curate value objects from the cited work itself.
evidence.quote: the application of an anodic potential induces two distinct pathways for Cu surface reconstruction: the reformation of surface oxides or the anodic dissolution

evidence.note: Second-hand: result reported by this review from Kok et al., JACS 2024 (ref 45); curate value objects from the cited work itself.
evidence.quote: enhance the duration of stable ethylene production by a factor of 20

props.scope: Cu-based CO2 electroreduction catalysts under pulsed electrolysis; in situ Raman plus electrochemical measurements by Kok et al., JACS 2024 (ref 45).
props.statement: Periodic anodic oxidation pulses stabilize Cu-based CO2RR catalysts by resetting the surface microenvironment: an applied anodic potential reforms surface oxides or dissolves Cu, and the subsequent cathodic step reduces the oxides or redeposits the dissolved Cu, continuously regenerating coordinatively unsaturated Cu active centres; this extends the duration of stable ethylene production by a factor of 20 but only mitigates, and cannot eradicate, catalyst failure by directional Cu dissolution and migration.

props.name: H-induced shifted-row reconstruction of Cu(100)

evidence.note: Second-hand: result reported by this review from Zhang et al., JACS 2022 (ref 37); curate value objects from the cited work itself.

creates 3-fold hollow sites with an exceptionally high binding affinity for hydrogen

props.scope: Cu(100) under electroreduction conditions; global optimization + GCDFT + AIMD by Zhang et al., JACS 2022 (ref 37).
props.statement: Hydrogen-induced "shifted-row reconstruction" of Cu(100) under electroreduction: H adsorption weakens the Cu-Cu bonds between topmost and subsurface layers and displaces Cu atomic rows, creating 3-fold hollow sites with exceptionally high hydrogen binding affinity that thermodynamically stabilize the distortion at elevated H coverage.

props.name: Tensile strain lowers CO2RR limiting potentials on Cu

evidence.note: Second-hand: result reported by this review from Du & An, J. Phys. Chem. C 2021 (ref 41); curate value objects from the cited work itself.
evidence.quote: tensile strain on facets like Cu(100) or Cu(211) can selectively lower the limiting potentials for distinct CO2RR pathways

props.scope: Cu(100) and Cu(211) facets under CO2RR; theoretical prediction reviewed here (ref 41).
props.statement: Theoretical simulations predict that specific degrees of tensile strain on facets such as Cu(100) or Cu(211) can selectively lower the limiting potentials of distinct CO2RR pathways; strain engineering is tied to reconstruction because atomic-scale restructuring is largely a stress-relief mechanism balancing intrinsic lattice strain and adsorbate-induced strain.

props.name: Wave-like Cu*CO diffusion, 0.10 eV barrier

evidence.note: Second-hand: result reported by this review from Zhang et al., JACS 2024 (ref 38); curate value objects from the cited work itself. The text layer drops the minus signs of the printed potential window (-0.5 to -1.0 VRHE).

props.scope: Cu electrodes under realistic reduction conditions, -0.5 to -1.0 VRHE; GCGA global optimization + quasi-kMC by Zhang et al., JACS 2024 (ref 38).
props.statement: Within about -0.5 to -1.0 VRHE, synergistic adsorbed *H and atop *CO drive dynamic surface roughening of Cu: metastable Cu*CO species diffuse by a "wave-like" propagation mechanism with a kinetic barrier as low as 0.10 eV and dimerize to form the actual active sites governing selective CO2 reduction to C2+ products.

props.statement: Operando EC-STM has captured a step-wise conversion of Cu(111) domains into a Cu(100)-like surface under prolonged cathodic polarization, which explains why polycrystalline Cu eventually shows Cu(100)-like C2+ selectivity.

props.scope: Cu8/g-C3N4 clusters, ML-GCMC/GCDFT at 0.00 to -1.00 VRHE; Zhu et al., JACS 2026 (ref 25).
props.statement: ML-accelerated GCMC and GCDFT on Cu8/g-C3N4 show potential-driven surface speciation: at 0.00 VRHE the Cu8 surface is predominantly covered by *HCOO, and as the potential shifts negatively (to -0.40 VRHE and below) *CO replaces *HCOO until a *CO-saturated Cu8(CO)15 complex forms at -1.00 VRHE; under operating potentials of -0.50 to -1.00 VRHE the *CO-saturated cluster is thermodynamically more stable than bulk Cu, and at -1.00 VRHE the lowest barrier for *CO-*CO coupling on Cu8(CO)15 is only 0.25 eV, following an atop-atop pathway distinct from the bridge-site pathway of Cu(100).

props.scope: CuO-derived Cu particles of 10-20 nm precursor size; Rollier et al., ACS Catal. 2024 (ref 7).
props.statement: Medium-sized CuO precursors (10-20 nm) were designed to control the electrochemistry-induced surface structures of the derived Cu particles; the surface defects created by reconstruction affect the competition between CO dimerization and the HER and thereby the product distribution.

props.name: Environment-reconstruction-performance framework

evidence.quote: we emphasize the importance of uncovering the dynamic structural evolutions of working electrocatalysts
bridging atomic-scale active interfaces with macroscopic catalytic performance

props.scope: CO2RR electrocatalysts generally; this review's unifying framework.
props.statement: Surface reconstruction is the central mechanistic link between the electrochemical environment (applied potential, local pH, electrolyte species) and CO2RR performance: coverage and reconstruction reorganize surface structure and electronics across length scales, and the reconstructed interfaces govern intermediate adsorption, stabilization and C-C coupling, hence reaction pathways and product distributions (the review's environment-reconstruction-performance framework, Fig. 8).
unmodeled: Fig. 8 is a schematic conceptual framework (reproduced/drawn, not data); its graphical content is not digitized

props.name: Three outlook priorities for reconstruction research

evidence.quote: the active implementation of pulsed electrolysis strategies can achieve the dynamic refreshing and regeneration of active sites

props.scope: Future directions for CO2RR reconstruction research, as proposed by this review.
props.statement: The review's outlook names three priorities: integrated in situ characterization with ultrahigh spatiotemporal (femtosecond-level temporal, atomic-level spatial) resolution under industrially relevant conditions; deepening machine-learning and multiscale simulation for mesoscopic/nanosecond dynamic evolution; and a shift from passive understanding to active steering of reconstruction, e.g. pulsed electrolysis to refresh and regenerate active sites and electrolyte/additive engineering to lock in favourable reconstructed configurations.

props.scope: Surface-P-doped Cu2O nanoparticles in CO2RR; Mao et al., ACS Nano 2025 (ref 18); the free energies are that work's calculations.
props.statement: In surface-P-doped Cu2O under CO2RR cathodic potentials, P binds lattice oxygen and desorbs into the electrolyte, extracting lattice O and rapidly generating a very high density of oxygen vacancies (XPS Olatt and Cu 2p shifts; in situ EPR shows the vacancies persist and grow with reduction time); the vacancy-rich microenvironment lowers the computed free energy of *O*CCO formation from 1.73 eV on Cu2O(200) to 1.11 eV on the fully reduced surface and enables a C2+ faradaic efficiency of 87.0% at a partial current density of 347.8 mA cm-2, with 46.1% FE(C2H4) and 31.5% FE(C2H5OH).

props.name: Field-corrected RHE-referenced Pourbaix needed

evidence.quote: the conventional approach is inherently linked to the standard hydrogen electrode (SHE) scale
Pt(111) exhibits H*-covered surfaces during the HER in acidic media
the pH-dependent diagram referenced to the RHE scale is considered more accurate

props.scope: Surface Pourbaix analysis of electrochemical interfaces, exemplified on Pt(111); field-corrected scheme by Liu et al., Langmuir 2024 (ref 70).
props.statement: Classical surface Pourbaix diagrams treat pH through a concentration-dependent proton correction and are therefore tied to the SHE scale while remaining RHE-scale-independent, which can contradict experiment at moderate-to-high pH (Pt(111) is H*-covered in acidic media but HO*-covered in alkaline media at the same RHE potential); a field-corrected, pH-dependent Pourbaix scheme that accounts for the electric field, adsorbate dipole/polarizability and the PZC reproduces the experimental trends and is considered more accurate.

props.statement: Large-scale data mining of the experimental CO2RR literature (DigCat database) shows a divergence among Sn oxides: mainstream SnO2-based catalysts, about 65% of the reported Sn-based materials, overwhelmingly favour HCOOH/HCOO- as the main C1 product, whereas rarely investigated SnO-based materials, only about 3% of the literature, co-produce HCOOH and CO in comparable ratios over a wide range of applied potentials.

props.scope: SnO2 and SnS2 under CO2RR conditions, active-learning MLP MD with HRTEM validation; Wang et al., Adv. Funct. Mater. 2025 (ref 24).
props.statement: ML-accelerated MD shows divergent reconstruction pathways for Sn compounds under cathodic polarization: SnO2 depletes lattice oxygen to near-complete reduction of the outermost layer and aggregates surface Sn into an anisotropic nanorod-like morphology (confirmed by HRTEM), while SnS2, driven by Sn-S bond cleavage and sulfur vacancies, evolves into a highly rough, disordered amorphous phase; the anion-vacancy-dominated reconstructed surfaces (SnO2-x(R), SnS2-x(R)) adsorb the *OCHO intermediate more favourably than the pristine stoichiometric surfaces, giving high HCOOH selectivity.

props.scope: SnO surfaces at about -0.7 to -1.4 V vs. RHE; surface Pourbaix + AIMD + constant-potential simulations by Guo et al., ACS Catal. 2025 (ref 11).
props.statement: Surface Pourbaix plus AIMD resolved the in situ resting state of SnO under CO2RR operating potentials (about -0.7 to -1.4 V vs. RHE): lattice-O migration in SnO has a prohibitively high barrier (2.25 eV), but oxygen vacancies become thermodynamically favourable under reduction via H2(OL)* intermediates, until a 1 ML OV* coverage fully terminates the layered surface and surface Sn turns from Sn2+ into electron-rich metallic Sn0 with Sn clusters; constant-potential simulations show pristine p-SnO binds *OCHO optimally but *COOH too weakly (trajectory diverted to *OCHO -> HCOOH), while the reconstructed r-SnO binds both *COOH and *OCHO strongly, so electrochemically induced vacancies and the accompanying reconstruction govern the dynamic HCOOH/HCOO- vs. CO product distribution.

low-coordinated Sn species (e.g., Sn2C, Sn3C, and Sn4C)

props.scope: SnO2-x surfaces under CO2 electrocatalysis; constrained genetic algorithm global search by Guo et al., Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2024 (ref 10).
props.statement: A constrained genetic algorithm search on SnO2-x surfaces shows oxygen vacancies convert surrounding Sn atoms into low-coordinated species (Sn2C, Sn3C, Sn4C) and ultimately build an electron-rich metallic Sn cluster layer (the "Sn layer"), the true active phase for HCOOH selectivity; HCOOH production proceeds most favourably on the reconstructed s-SnO2-x(110) surface, with a substantially lowered barrier for the potential-determining initial hydrogenation step.
